stem: For the linear function \(f\), \(f(4) = 9\), and the graph of \(y = f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane crosses the \(x\)-axis at \(x = 10\). What is the value of \(f(0)\)?
solution: The graph passes through \((4, 9)\) and \((10, 0)\), so the slope is \(\frac{0 - 9}{10 - 4} = -\frac{3}{2}\).
From \(x = 4\) back to \(x = 0\), \(x\) decreases by 4, so \(f(x)\) increases by \(4 \cdot \frac{3}{2} = 6\).
verify:
x = symbols('x')
m = Rational(0 - 9, 10 - 4)
f = 9 + m*(x - 4)
assert f.subs(x, 10) == 0 and f.subs(x, 0) == 15
assert [Rational(s) for s in spr_answers] == [f.subs(x, 0)]
